summary: Two blind readers preferred the pre-revision draft (medium and medium-low confidence). The revision removed the named register defects but cut argumentative hinges with the ornament, and introduced a few errors. Repair by restoring the argument in plain form, never by restoring the removed ornaments.

findings.problem: Explanations that taught the argument were cut with the maxims: why Jerome's Philippians key matters (the earlier draft: read without it, texts of receiving make the Son a creature promoted for his merits; read with it, they speak of what the eternal Son receives in the nature he took); the point of Aquinas's double right (the Son does not ask because he lacks; he asks because the Father wills that even what is owed be received as a gift, and because the asking is his passion).
findings.required_result: Restore each as a plain step of the argument attributed to its author, without 'removes the scandal' or a closing maxim. A 'not X' clause is legitimate here only where the text itself raises X (the eternal Son's asking does raise it).

findings.problem: The interpretation lost its question and two explanations: the framing that the Gospel's denial read alone could empty the Collect's subjection of public consequence while the Gradual read alone could make Christ Caesar's rival (now the Quas primas sentence stands orphaned as a one-sentence paragraph); Aquinas's 'it is here, because it is everywhere' explained (a kingdom whose origin is one place in the world is bounded by that place; one whose origin is above is bounded by none); 'Both statements are Augustine's.' Also: 'In the Gospel the bound prisoner says his kingdom is not \latin{de} this world' (30:230) is a mixed Latin-English slip; 'Of the kingdom itself he says: "Those who believe in Him," who were…' is an ungrammatical splice; 'Augustine, Aquinas, Bellarmine and Theodoret also say what the kings and nations… are to do' is a bare roster.
findings.required_result: State the question plainly with who holds or invites each misreading (Quas primas names one error itself) and attach the Quas primas sentence to it; restore the Aquinas explanation attributed to him; restore 'Both statements are Augustine's' where it applies; fix the Latin slip and the splice; replace the roster with what those authors say.

findings.location: sections/20, 30, 40 the walks through the texts; sections/50-comparison.tex
findings.problem: New tics: 'on this interpretation', 'taken this way', 'this interpretation takes' repeated through the walks until they flatten them; inert sentences ('The Communion's Sedebit Dominus Rex in aeternum is taken here of the exalted King.'; 'The Secret asks for all nations the gifts of unity and peace.'). The comparison stops on the two-births sentence without a conclusion, and its 'would mislead on its own' comparative work was cut rather than made plain.
findings.required_result: In the walks, say for each text what it says and why it matters to this interpretation's argument, marking the study's inference in ordinary, varied words only where one is drawn. End the comparison with a short conclusion that says concretely what each interpretation accounts for that the others leave aside and how the three meet in the Preface's sentence, as content.

findings.problem: Keep the revision's gains that both readers credited: 'Neither speaks of the Postcommunion…' (honest about where the Fathers stop), the paragraph on the three interpretations' different times, the plainer Jn 18:37 paragraph, the plain headings, 'authors' for 'witnesses'.
